items.headline: The 2026 budget is out. MPs are debating it before a vote.
items.short_title: The 2026 budget is being debated before a confidence vote
items.what: The Finance Minister presented the government's yearly spending and tax plan on November 5. The House is now debating it. One proposed change to the budget motion has already been voted down.
items.you: The budget sets what Ottawa spends on things like housing and health care. The final budget vote is a [[confidence|confidence vote]]: if it fails, it could trigger an election.

sides.text: Calls it a plan to grow the economy and attract investment, including funding aimed at ending homelessness within 10 years.
Say it adds too much debt, pointing to $765 billion in new debt over five years.
Object that it slows the growth of health care money sent to provinces, from 5% to 3% a year starting in 2028.
Raised concerns about spending on fossil fuels and benefits for corporations.

items.sides_note: Listed in order of seats held. These are what each party said in the House, not checked facts.

poll.q: Your take: would you vote for this budget?
poll.reveal: **What actually happens:** the final vote hasn't happened yet. Check back here to see how it goes.

items.headline: MPs back changes to medically assisted dying rules, moving the bill to committee
items.short_title: Assisted dying bill passes first vote, heads to committee
items.what: It would permanently rule out medical assistance in dying when a mental illness is the only condition. It would also let people with illnesses that may later take away their ability to decide make a request in advance, in provinces that set up a system for it.
items.you: A small group of MPs will study the bill in detail and can suggest changes. Nothing has changed in the law yet.

sides.text: Say it adds safeguards, including independent medical assessments and the ability to withdraw consent.
Doubt the bill would hold up in court as written and say it could be more restrictive than current rules.

items.sides_note: Before the vote, the government used [[time-allocation|time allocation]] to limit how long debate could run.

poll.q: Your take: should this bill move forward?
poll.reveal: **What actually happened:** MPs voted to move it forward. It's now in committee.

items.headline: The federal gas tax break is extended into 2027
items.short_title: Gas tax break is law until early 2027
items.what: The federal excise tax on fuel stays off until the end of January 2027. It comes back at half rate in February and March, then returns in full in April 2027.
items.you: You keep paying less federal tax at the pump through winter. Expect prices to step up in February and again in April 2027.

sides.text: Call it temporary relief while global fuel prices are high.
Call it a half-measure, since the tax comes back in 2027, and want it cut for good.

poll.reveal: **What actually happened:** it passed both the House and Senate and became law in late October.

items.headline: A bill to make cell coverage maps more accurate nears its final House vote
items.short_title: Cell coverage map bill nears final House vote
items.what: It would require checks on the mobile coverage data that providers report, plus regular reviews of how Canada manages wireless airwaves.
items.you: Coverage maps decide where money goes to fix weak service, so accurate data matters most in rural areas.

sides.text: MPs who spoke in debate supported it. No party has come out against it.

items.sides_note: This is a [[pmb|private member's bill]], not a government bill.

poll.reveal: **What actually happens:** the final House vote is still to come. With support from every party, it's likely to pass.
